The verifier did not pass. The cube is jammed tilted in the pocket mouth and I have no way left to move it, so I stopped and returned the arm home.

**What happened**

- The grasp went cleanly. I matched the wrist roll to the cube's yaw, closed on it with the centre half a millimetre off the jaw line, and lifted it.
- Over the tray I set the roll so the cube's yaw matched the pocket and lowered it. On the first descent the held cube clipped the funnel and tilted in the grip, so I raised it until it read flat again.
- I released it from just above the funnel top, flat and close to centre. It did not slide in. It wedged with one bottom edge on the pocket floor and the other on the lead-in rim.

Verifier reading after release and at the end:

| Check | Value | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| Distance from slot centre | 4.1 mm | 3 mm |
| Tilt | 32.7° | 5° |
| Height error | 3.8 mm | 1 mm |

**Why I could not recover it**

- The grasp rule rejects any cube tilted more than 10°, so it cannot be re-picked.
- Pushing it with the fingers has no effect. I pressed down on its high side, pushed it sideways, and swept a jaw through it. The fingertips passed well inside the cube's volume each time and the cube never moved, so finger-to-cube contact is not simulated. Only a grasp can move it, and a grasp is ruled out by the tilt.

**What is needed next**

The scene has to be reset to free the cube. On the next attempt I would not rely on the funnel. I would lower the held cube directly to the seated height while correcting position from the read-back pose, and only release once it is in the pocket.

I could not save notes to memory because no file-writing tool is available in this session.
